concepts.def: Slide a shape without rotating or reflecting; described by a vector.
Flip across a mirror line; the image is the same distance behind the line.
Turn around a centre by an angle; clockwise or anticlockwise.
Scale a shape from a centre by a scale factor; if negative, also reflects.
Same shape and size — translations, reflections and rotations produce congruent images.
Same shape but possibly different size — enlargement produces similar images.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Transformations & Vectors — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Transformations & Vectors brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Transformations & Vectors.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which transformation can change the size of a shape?
options: translation
reflection
rotation
enlargement
a vector
a centre and angle
a mirror line
a scale factor

mcqs.q: How does the graph of y = f(x - 3) compare to y = f(x)?
options: 1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.
It is reflected in the y-axis because of the minus.
It is translated 3 units to the right.
It is translated 3 units to the left because of the minus.

mcqs.q: If you've flipped a fair coin and got heads 5 times in a row, what is the probability the next flip is heads?
options: It is reflected in the y-axis because of the minus.
1/2 — each flip is independent of the previous ones.
Less than 1/2, because the coin is 'due' to land on tails to balance the results.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.

mcqs.q: A price increases by 20% then decreases by 20%. Is the final price the same as the original?
options: Yes — a 20% rise and a 20% fall cancel out exactly.
Yes — percentage changes always cancel because they are symmetric.
No — the final price is 96% of the original (a 4% net decrease), because each percentage is applied to a different base.
1 because the coin has clearly been biased by the previous flips.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rotation”?
options: Slide a shape without rotating or reflecting; described by a vector.
Scale a shape from a centre by a scale factor; if negative, also reflects.
Turn around a centre by an angle; clockwise or anticlockwise.
Same shape but possibly different size — enlargement produces similar images.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Reflection”?
options: Slide a shape without rotating or reflecting; described by a vector.
Scale a shape from a centre by a scale factor; if negative, also reflects.
Flip across a mirror line; the image is the same distance behind the line.
Turn around a centre by an angle; clockwise or anticlockwise.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Congruent shape”?
options: Scale a shape from a centre by a scale factor; if negative, also reflects.
Slide a shape without rotating or reflecting; described by a vector.
Same shape but possibly different size — enlargement produces similar images.
Same shape and size — translations, reflections and rotations produce congruent images.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Similar shape”?
options: Scale a shape from a centre by a scale factor; if negative, also reflects.
Same shape but possibly different size — enlargement produces similar images.
Slide a shape without rotating or reflecting; described by a vector.
Turn around a centre by an angle; clockwise or anticlockwise.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Enlargement”?
options: Turn around a centre by an angle; clockwise or anticlockwise.
Same shape but possibly different size — enlargement produces similar images.
Scale a shape from a centre by a scale factor; if negative, also reflects.
Flip across a mirror line; the image is the same distance behind the line.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Translation”?
options: Slide a shape without rotating or reflecting; described by a vector.
Same shape and size — translations, reflections and rotations produce congruent images.
Turn around a centre by an angle; clockwise or anticlockwise.
Scale a shape from a centre by a scale factor; if negative, also reflects.

mcqs.q: Enlarge a 4 cm line by scale factor 3. New length?
options: 11 cm
14 cm
9 cm
12 cm
